items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to unveil candidates on Oct 18, says Anwar’s aide
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will announce its candidates for the Melaka state election on October 18, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expected to personally unveil the line-up, said his political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin. Azman said the venue for the announcement would be announced at a later date. On speculation that he would contest the Paya Rumput seat in the election, Azman said he would leave the matter to the party leadership.

items.title: Haze: All schools in Johor, four Selangor districts closed tomorrow, says Fadhlina
items.summary: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the four district education offices covered the areas of Bangsar Pudu, Hulu Langat, Gombak and Petaling Perdana. "For Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, schools under PPDs (district education offices) other than those stated will also operate as usual," she said. She said state education directors have been told to set up a Haze Monitoring Task Force involving the state education departments and district education offices.

items.title: Haze: Johor postpones special school admission test; schools remain shut until Oct 16
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Special School Admission Assessment (PKSK), scheduled for tomorrow, has been postponed due to the haze, with a new date to be announced by the Johor Education Department. The assessment is used for admission to selected special schools, and the postponement follows the state's extension of school closures until Oct 16 to protect pupils' health and safety. Johor Education and Information Committee chairman, Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali, said the five-day closure extension was necessary amid deteriorating air quality.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, N. Sembilan, Pahang, Putrajaya and parts of KL, Selangor to reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang and Putrajaya, as well as several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, will resume normal operations tomorrow. In KUALA LUMPUR, the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said MOE educational institutions under the Sentul and Keramat District Education Offices (PPDs) would reopen tomorrow, following a decline in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the areas for three consecutive days. In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the Negeri Sembilan Education Department also said all MOE educational institutions would operate as usual tomorrow based on the latest air quality monitoring.

items.title: HRD Corp to support 3 million training opportunities under 2027 Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) will continue to utilise RM3 billion from its levy funds to support three million training opportunities, in line with the government's efforts to strengthen skills development and workforce competitiveness. HRD Corp said the measures supported the 13th Malaysia Plan's (13MP) target of having skilled workers make up 35 per cent of the workforce by 2030. He said HRD Corp would continue to focus on industry-relevant training, recognise professional certifications and the strategic utilisation of levy funds to ensure employers' investments in skills development delivered meaningful value to workers and businesses.

items.title: Haze: Air quality in Kuching, Miri improves to moderate levels, says DOE
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 11 — Air quality in Kuching and Miri has improved but remains in the moderate category, according to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index of Malaysia (APIMS) portal on Sunday. Kuching’s Air Pollutant Index (API) reading last recorded an unhealthy level at 2am today, at 111, before dropping to 99 at 3am. The reading subsequently declined from 153 at 3pm yesterday (Oct 10) to 85 at 3pm today, placing Kuching in the moderate category.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, Negri, Pahang, Putrajaya to reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Pahang and Putrajaya, as well as several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, will resume normal operations tomorrow. In KUALA LUMPUR, the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said MOE educational institutions under the Sentul and Keramat District Education Offices (PPDs) would reopen tomorrow, following a decline in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the areas for three consecutive days. In a statement, the department also said all schools in other districts in the state would operate as usual tomorrow.

items.title: Fama to add 241 agri-food outlets under 13MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) will expand its agri-food marketing network with 241 new outlets under the 13th Malaysia Plan. Fama senior director of market institutions division Intan Suraya Ibeni Hajar said the rejuvenation programme goes beyond upgrading the physical appearance of its outlets, emphasising building a modern business ecosystem. The 241 new outlets will comprise various marketing channels.

items.title: Digital tools, AI can preserve Dusun language for future generations, says Sabah deputy CM
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — Digital technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), has the potential to become a crucial medium in efforts to preserve the Dusun language, ensuring that this community’s heritage continues to be learned, used, and inherited by future generations. Sabah Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said that modern technology can be leveraged through the development of digital dictionaries, recordings of Dusun speech, podcast production, and the creation of online learning materials. He noted that these efforts need to be strengthened through the involvement of the younger generation, educational institutions, and local communities so that the Dusun language remains relevant and continues to be used in daily life.

items.title: Tax breaks, wage hike headline 2027 Budget surprises: CIMB Securities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget has delivered larger-than-expected tax relief and a higher minimum wage, offering support for household spending while raising cost pressures for businesses, said CIMB Securities. CIMB Securities analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang said the measures could generate annual tax savings of up to RM1,600 for about five million taxpayers, supporting middle-income consumption. Group (M) Bhd and QL Resources Bhd.

items.title: TH depositors' money not used to fund Perkeso for religious workers - Zulkifli
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said that Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) depositors' savings were not used to pay Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for 40,000 mosque personnel and takmir teachers nationwide. He said a special government allocation fully funded the contributions, channeled through TH as the implementing agency. Zulkifli said the government's decision to fully fund the contributions recognises religious personnel's service and helps safeguard their welfare, social protection and wellbeing.

items.title: Negri Sembilan schools to reopen tomorrow as air quality improves
items.summary: SEREMBAN: All Education Ministry (MOE) educational institutions in Negri Sembilan will resume normal operations tomorrow following a temporary closure last Friday due to poor air quality. In a statement today, the Negri Sembilan Education Department said the decision was made after monitoring prevailing weather conditions and the latest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. "The department wishes to inform that all MOE educational institutions in Negri Sembilan will operate as usual on Monday, Oct 12 based on the monitoring of current conditions and the latest API readings," the statement read.

items.title: FIA sees bigger motorsport role for Malaysia beyond F1
items.summary: THE successful return to the Formula 1 (F1) spotlight at Sepang has put Malaysia's motorsport credentials back on the global stage and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem believes the chequered flag should be only the beginning. Rather than chasing an F1 comeback alone, Malaysia has the ingredients to become a broader motorsport hub, drawing on its established racing culture, passionate fan base and growing pool of enthusiasts, he said. Malaysia, to me, is about motorsport," Ben Sulayem told the New Straits Times and three other media a few hours before the rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last Sunday.

items.title: M'sia condemns deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia, urges peaceful resolution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has strongly condemned the deadly attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia on Saturday (Oct 10), which claimed lives, left several people injured and disrupted airport operations and commercial flights. In a statement on Sunday, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said 12 people were killed and 309 injured in Saturday's attack on the King Khalid International Airport. Earlier, Malaysia's Foreign Ministry reported that there were no Malaysian casualties following Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a projectile landing near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

items.title: US activists deploy poll volunteers over Trump intimidation fears
items.summary: US civil rights and pro-democracy groups have begun sending out trained volunteers to counter the possible deployment of armed federal agents to polling locations ahead of next month's midterm elections. The Vote Safe initiative, launched as early voting began in Ohio this week, accuses President Donald Trump's administration of suppressing turnout by repeatedly raising the possibility of federal intervention around an election that could strip Republicans of control of Congress. Organisers say volunteers will explain voting rights, try to de-escalate confrontations and document potential intimidation or other misconduct.

items.title: Pahang schools to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
items.summary: KUANTAN: All schools in Pahang will operate as usual tomorrow despite the haze, the Pahang Education Department said. In a statement today, the department said any changes would be communicated from time to time through the respective district education offices, depending on developments in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. "The safety, health and welfare of pupils and the education community remain the department's priority," it said.

items.title: Firefly cancels Subang-Seletar flights over haze, weather concerns
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Firefly has cancelled all scheduled flights between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport in Singapore from Oct 10 to 12 as a precautionary safety measure due to weather and haze conditions. "Affected passengers are being contacted and reallocated onto available Malaysia Airlines services via the Kuala Lumpur Singapore route, subject to seat availability. The airline said it was also closely monitoring developments amid the evolving weather situation.

items.title: 'They can no longer blame DAP': Loke distances party from MB motion
items.summary: SEREMBAN: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has denied the party's involvement in any plan to table a no-confidence motion against Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, saying the party is focused on serving the people. The Transport Minister said DAP leaders were no longer part of the state administration and were concentrating on their responsibilities outside the government. Loke was responding to rumours of a no-confidence motion against Ismail at the next state assembly sitting.

items.title: RM260mil to strengthen disaster preparedness next year
items.summary: IPOH: The government will allocate RM260 million to the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) next year to strengthen disaster preparedness, including providing essential equipment for rescue operations. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the allocation would help address equipment shortages among agencies involved in disaster response, including boats, water pumps and water filtration machines. He said the equipment was crucial not only for rescue operations but also to ensure access to clean water when disasters disrupted water supplies.

items.title: 'Maybe they don't need our help': Malaysia awaits Indonesia on haze aid
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the offer was conveyed directly to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka during his recent official visit to Jakarta. He said Malaysia was prepared to deploy a water-bombing aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to assist firefighting operations in Kalimantan. However, he said preventive measures and coordination through regional cooperation should take priority over legal action.

items.title: Ahmad Maslan confident Umno will cooperate with Pas in Melaka election
items.summary: JASIN: Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan is confident that Barisan Nasional (BN) will reach a political understanding with Pas for the Melaka state election to advance Muslim unity. "Negotiations are still ongoing, but I am confident Umno will cooperate with Pas in the Melaka state election. Also present were former Jasin MP Datuk Seri Ahmad Hamzah, Jasin Umno deputy division chief Datuk Azman Abdullah and former Serkam assemblyman Datuk Zaidi Attan.

items.title: Budget 2027: Socso offers up to RM150 tax relief for Lindung 24 Jam, Lindung Kendiri contributors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Contributors who remain under the Lindung 24 Jam Scheme, as well as those making mandatory contributions to the Lindung Kendiri Scheme, will be eligible for additional tax relief of up to RM150 under Budget 2027. The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), in a statement today, said the initiative is expected to benefit more than 8.5 million Lindung 24 Jam contributors and 1.7 million Lindung Kendiri contributors. Under Budget 2027, e-hailing and p-hailing workers will also receive a 35 per cent matching contribution from Perkeso, with the rate increasing to 50 per cent if platform companies also contribute towards their social security payments.

items.title: Kelantan Syariah Court confirms divorce after man stabs wife
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Syariah High Court today confirmed a cerai taklik after ruling that a man had breached his conditional divorce pronouncement by stabbing his wife six times on Oct 5. "After hearing the defendant's admission, the court today ruled in favour of the plaintiff's claim and confirmed the 'taklik' divorce. "The court found that the defendant had breached the 'taklik' pronouncement made during their marriage about six years ago by stabbing the plaintiff six times, causing her serious injuries.

items.title: South Korea completes trial of Arctic shipping route
items.summary: SEOUL: A South Korean container ship returned on Sunday from a trial voyage through the Arctic, testing an alternative route opened by melting sea ice as conflict in the Middle East disrupts global shipping. The Arctic route could also expose operators to sanctions-related risks because it runs along Russia's northern coast. Environmental advocates, however, warn that expanded commercial shipping along the Northern Sea Route could threaten the fragile Arctic ecosystem.

items.title: Budget 2027: Nadma to use RM260m allocation for disaster relief centres, equipment, says Zahid
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) will prioritise the RM260 million allocated under Budget 2027 for establishing more Permanent Disaster Relief Centres (PPKBs) and procuring disaster preparedness assets and equipment, said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. “We want to establish two permanent disaster relief centres in each state. Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said this at a press conference after launching the 2026 National Preparedness Month (BKN) at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.

items.title: Health Ministry steps up efforts to recruit, retain nurses amid overseas migration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is expediting nurse recruitment and strengthening efforts to retain those already in service through improved welfare support and career advancement opportunities to address the migration of nurses abroad. Dzulkefly said other measures included maintaining the 42-hour working week for nurses on shift duty, expanding training and promotion opportunities, and offering greater flexibility in placements through a mutual exchange system. Dzulkefly said the MOH no longer recruited nurses on a contract basis, with all new recruits offered permanent appointments.

items.title: Mindef eyes idle military land for food security, veterans' welfare
items.summary: Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the JanaVeteran Programme, in collaboration with Boustead Plantations (BPlant), could help achieve this objective. "So we want BPlant to help the country strengthen food security," he said at a press conference after launching JanaKomuniti at Felda Air Tawar 3 here today. Khaled said food security must be taken seriously, as supply shortages or rising food costs could escalate into a national security threat.

items.title: Selangor career carnival offers 3,568 jobs for vulnerable groups
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 11 — The Selangor government has expanded job opportunities for vulnerable groups through the Selangor JobCare Istimewa Career Carnival 2026, which offers 3,568 vacancies. State Human Resources and Poverty Eradication Committee chairman V. Papparaidu said the state government was aware of the challenges faced by these groups in entering the job market, particularly persons with disabilities (OKU), Orang Asli, military veterans and senior citizens. “The 3,568 positions available include 1,603 vacancies for Orang Asli, veterans (1,333), OKU (472) and senior citizens (160).

items.title: Imran Khan's party's provincial government suspended by Pakistan president
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan's president suspended the government in a province ruled by the party of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan after declaring a state of emergency on Sunday, his office said, stripping its elected administration of its powers. The decision comes amid a confrontation between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government and Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, which governs northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. President Asif Ali Zardari signed Sharif's advice to declare a state of emergency following a federal cabinet decision, his office said in a statement.

items.title: Pakatan targets Tampin parliamentary seat comeback in next GE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is aiming to reclaim the Tampin parliamentary seat at the next general election, with its election machinery urged to strengthen its efforts and engage voters from now. Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) deputy president Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said all parties must work harder to restore public confidence and demonstrate PH’s capabilities through its administrative performance and service to the community, Kosmo! Aminuddin, who is also Negeri Sembilan PH chairman, said winning back Tampin should be one of the coalition’s main priorities as it prepares for the general election, which is expected to be held in October or November next year.

items.title: Rehda asks stamp duty relief for homes up to RM1mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rehda Malaysia has urged the government to extend stamp duty exemptions to first-time buyers of homes priced up to RM1 million. Its president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the proposed measures under the 2027 Budget will ease upfront costs but called for the eligibility threshold to reflect prevailing house prices, particularly in high-cost urban areas. Under the measures, first-time buyers will receive full stamp duty exemptions on instruments of transfer and loan agreements for properties priced up to RM500,000.

items.title: Zahid: Disaster preparedness key to reducing property losses
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 11 — Preparedness in disaster management helps reduce property losses, including damage to public assets and infrastructure, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said that losses due to disasters in the country last year reached RM636.9 million, including RM380.2 million involving public assets and infrastructure. We want to raise public awareness of the importance of National Preparedness Month (BKN) in building the capacity to address potential risks before disaster strikes,” said Ahmad Zahid, who also chairs the Central Disaster Management Committee.

items.title: Health Ministry to expedite permanent appointments for contract pharmacists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is committed to expediting the absorption of contract pharmacists into permanent positions through close cooperation with the Finance Ministry and the government. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said that, as of July, 3,545 pharmacists were still serving on contract under the ministry, while another 115 were on the reserve list for permanent appointments. Meanwhile, Dzulkefly confirmed that there were no longer any contract nurses in the public healthcare service, with all nurses now offered permanent positions.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Perak, Negeri Sembilan to reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Schools in three Perak districts and educational institutions across Negeri Sembilan will resume normal operations tomorrow, following reviews of air quality and prevailing conditions. Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said schools in Kinta Utara, Kinta Selatan and Kuala Kangsar could reopen after Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at all monitoring stations in the state remained below 150 as of 2pm today, according to a report by national news agency Bernama. In Negeri Sembilan, the state Education Department said all educational institutions under its jurisdiction would operate as usual on Monday after reviewing the latest API readings and current conditions.

items.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder says PM Modi an 'embarrassment'
items.summary: NEW DELHI: The founder of India's online "cockroach" movement said on Sunday Prime Minister Narendra Modi was an "embarrassment" to the country, soon after being released from detention. "Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India," Abhijeet Dipke said in a social media post. "Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully," said the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder, who was detained on Saturday before planned protests over electoral roll revisions.

items.title: Cell Broadcast System in final phase to deliver disaster alerts to phones
items.summary: IPOH: The Cell Broadcast System, a national disaster warning system announced last year, is in its final phase of development, with live testing scheduled for Nov 19. "Through this system, warnings can be sent directly to mobile phones in areas at risk without interfering with or accessing personal data," Zahid said. The system transmits alerts through mobile networks to compatible devices in designated areas.

items.title: Melaka schools reopen tomorrow as API readings dip below 100, says state exco
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 11 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education in Melaka will reopen tomorrow (October 12) after the Air Pollutant Index (API) recorded moderate readings below 100. State Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman said the decision took into account the latest air quality developments and prioritised the education, safety and well-being of students, teachers and all members of educational institutions. Based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Melaka recorded moderate API readings as of 2 pm today: Alor Gajah (91), Bukit Rambai (94) and Bandaraya Melaka (96).

items.title: #NSTviral: 'GTA-style' chaos as man flees cops, grabs motorcycle in Wangsa Maju [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man who attempted to flee from a police officer after his pickup truck crashed into a road median in Wangsa Maju was caught on video attempting to escape on a motorcycle before being subdued by the officer and several motorists. In the first clip posted by user @tqriz.hykl on Threads, the man was seen dashing away from the policeman and the orange pickup truck, before crashing into a motorcyclist who had got off his motorcycle at an intersection. The man then ran across the opposing lane into traffic, with the policeman close behind, towards the roadside.

items.title: Haze: Malaysia still awaiting Indonesia’s response to firefighting aid offer, says DPM Zahid
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 11 — Malaysia is still awaiting a response from Indonesia on its offer to help put out forest and land fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan that have caused transboundary haze, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. In his speech, Ahmad Zahid, who is also chairman of the National Disaster Management Committee, said Malaysia had offered a firefighting aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel to assist with firefighting operations in Indonesia. Meanwhile, he said the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) not only assisted in managing disasters domestically but was also always ready to provide aid to other countries affected by disasters.

items.title: EP Manufacturing, China partner invest RM100mil in Proton fuel tanks plant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: EP Manufacturing Bhd has partnered with China's Hebei Shichang Auto Parts Co Ltd to invest RM100 million in a new fuel-tank manufacturing facility to supply Proton Holdings Bhd. The joint venture supports Proton's expansion plans while strengthening Malaysia's local automotive component supply chain and its potential as a regional manufacturing and export hub. Under an agreement signed on Oct 9, EP Manufacturing will hold a 51 per cent stake in the joint venture company, EP Shichang Automotive Systems Sdn Bhd, while Hebei Shichang will own the remaining 49 per cent.

items.title: Zahid wants states to implement Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030
items.summary: IPOH: States must translate the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030 into concrete action plans based on local risks, with clear responsibilities and implementation targets. Zahid said both scenarios required early preparation and close coordination among government agencies to minimise risks and protect lives. "I want every state to translate the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030 into action plans according to local risks, with clear agency responsibilities and implementation targets.

items.title: Melaka schools to reopen tomorrow as haze improves
items.summary: MELAKA: All schools in Melaka will reopen tomorrow after being closed for a day due to haze. Melaka Education Department director Mahfudzah Mohamed Noor said the decision was made following an improvement in air quality, with the latest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings returning to healthy levels. She said the decision also took into account prevailing conditions, while prioritising the safety and well-being of pupils, teachers and education institution staff.

items.title: Budget 2027: Digital Ministry targets 200,000 AI-skilled individuals in push for AI Nation by 2030
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — The Ministry of Digital is intensifying efforts to strengthen the nation’s digital ecosystem, empower local tech talent and build a future-ready workforce under Budget 2027, as part of Malaysia’s broader ambition to become an AI Nation by 2030. In a statement today, the Ministry said these efforts include producing 200,000 AI-skilled individuals by strengthening AI Malaysia Bhd, with a focus on developing high-skilled talent, digital infrastructure and efficient, secure and ethical AI governance. “The Fifth Madani Budget, themed “Menggapai Di Langit, Mengakar Di Bumi” (Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values), tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last Friday, reflects the government’s bold commitment to driving the nation’s digital transformation towards an AI Nation, anchored in the inclusive Malaysia Digital framework,” the statement read.

items.title: Defence Ministry to use idle military land for food security, veteran welfare, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the JanaVeteran Programme, in collaboration with Boustead Plantations (BPlant), could carry out this programme. “So we want BPlant to help the country strengthen food security,” he said at a press conference after launching JanaKomuniti at Felda Air Tawar 3 here today. Mohamad said food security must be given serious attention, as supply shortages or rising food costs could escalate into a national security threat.

items.title: Perak schools to resume normal operations tomorrow
items.summary: IPOH: Schools in Perak will resume normal operations tomorrow as air pollutant index (API) readings across the state remain below 150. Perak Education Department director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar said the decision was made following improvements in air quality, with all monitoring stations in the state recording API readings below the unhealthy threshold of 150 as of 2pm today. "Therefore, all educational institutions under the Education Ministry in Perak will operate as usual from Oct 12," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia in high-level contact over haze as Jakarta deploys 60,000 to fight fires, says Indonesian minister
items.summary: JAKARTA, Oct 11 — Indonesia and Malaysia have maintained high-level diplomatic communication over transboundary haze caused by forest and land fires, following a telephone conversation between their leaders amid concerns over worsening air pollution. Indonesian Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir said he had spoken to his Malaysian counterpart Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, to explain Indonesia’s firefighting efforts. According to the ministry’s monitoring system, Central Kalimantan recorded the highest number, at 288, followed by South Sumatra (60), West Kalimantan (44), South Kalimantan (28) and Jambi (one), while Riau recorded none.

items.title: Claims that Tabung Haji depositors’ money funded Socso contributions for religious workers untrue, says Zulkifli Hasan
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said that Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) depositors’ savings were not used to pay Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributions for 40,000 mosque personnel and takmir teachers nationwide. He said a special government allocation fully funded the contributions, channeled through TH as the implementing agency. Zulkifli said the government’s decision to fully fund the contributions recognises religious personnel’s service and helps safeguard their welfare, social protection and wellbeing.

items.title: ‘Negeri Sembilan crisis is not DAP’s fault’, says Anthony Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — DAP has stressed that it is not responsible for the ongoing political crisis in Negeri Sembilan. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said it was unfair to continue blaming the party for the crisis when it was no longer part of the state government, according to a report by Sinar Harian today. During the Negeri Sembilan state election campaign, they tried to link DAP to the crisis, claiming that we were responsible for what was happening in the state.

items.title: JPJ suspends Chery Omoda 5 approval, new registrations after rear axle incident in Johor Bahru
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) has temporarily suspended the Vehicle Type Approval (VTA) for the affected Chery Omoda 5 model and variants following a safety concern arising from an incident that went viral in Johor Bahru last week. JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the action also involved a suspension of new registrations for the vehicles until technical investigations were completed and the safety risks identified, Kosmo! “JPJ views seriously the viral incident involving a Chery Omoda 5 in Johor Bahru last week, which raised public concerns over the safety of the vehicle.

items.title: Budget 2027: PTPTN offers 10pc discount to borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments will enjoy a 10 per cent discount from 2027. PTPTN chairman Datuk Seri Norliza Abdul Rahim said the incentive was a form of recognition for borrowers who demonstrated discipline in fulfilling their loan repayment obligations. She said the government has announced an initiative to defer PTPTN loan repayments in 2027, which would benefit more than 400,000 borrowers, as well as a minimum monthly repayment of RM50 for low-income borrowers.

items.title: LCS 1 completion not tied to RCI, shipbuilder told to speed up work, says defence minister
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 11 — The establishment of a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) to investigate delays in the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project is not a determining factor in ensuring the prompt completion of the country’s defence asset. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the shipbuilder had been instructed to expedite work and ensure that further delays did not occur. Otherwise, the ship would still not be completed.

items.title: Employers urged to use job coaches to support workers with disabilities, says deputy minister
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 11 — Employers are urged to leverage Job Coach services to help workers with disabilities (PwD) adapt to their duties and work environment, thereby expanding inclusive employment opportunities. Deputy Minister of Women, Family and Community Development Lim Hui Ying said the services would also help employers understand the needs of PwD workers and adopt appropriate communication methods to ensure they could perform their duties effectively. She said with appropriate guidance, workplace adjustments and mutual understanding, more persons with disabilities could perform well at work and contribute productively.

items.title: Selangor Sultan officiates renaming of Morib square after former MB Harun Idris
items.summary: BANTING, Oct 11 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today officiated the renaming of Dataran Morib to Dataran Dato’ Seri Harun Idris at Pantai Morib here. Also present was the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, while Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari accompanied the Sultan during the ceremony. In a statement, Kuala Langat Municipal Council (MPKL) said the square officially reopened to the public today following the completion of the RM60.50 million Morib Beach Conservation Project on July 1.

items.title: Riyadh airport attack: No evacuation needed for Malaysian students in Saudi Arabia for now, says Zambry
items.summary: LUMUT, Oct 11 — There is currently no urgent need to evacuate Malaysian students in Saudi Arabia, but close monitoring is being carried out following yesterday’s attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said monitoring was being conducted in several areas, particularly Madinah and Makkah, to prevent any risks that could threaten the students’ safety. He said the assistance, channelled through Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS), covered students at public universities, teacher education institutes (IPGs), matriculation colleges, polytechnics and other institutions.

items.title: Teo Nie Ching: RM300m smart city project to transform Kota Kinabalu by 2028
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — Kota Kinabalu is set to be transformed into a smart city through a project worth about RM300 million, expected to be completed by February 2028, enhancing urban management, public safety and service delivery. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the Kota Kinabalu Smart City Project, which began on August 6, was being implemented through a collaboration between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK), using Universal Service Provision (USP) funds. She said the project involved developing fibre-optic and public Wi-Fi networks, including 50 kilometres of backbone network and 308 kilometres of last-mile network, installing 822 smart poles and multi-purpose poles, and establishing a Network Operations Command Centre (NOCC).

items.title: Pahang retiree loses over RM1.1m in TikTok-promoted investment scam
items.summary: Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the 65-year-old man saw an advertisement before contacting someone who claimed to represent the company through WhatsApp. He said the victim was briefed on stock investments and financial market analysis before agreeing to join the scheme. Azry Akmar said the victim was asked to make further payments even after completing all the transactions.

items.title: Nanta urges Kapit community groups to ensure transparent use of aid
items.summary: KAPIT, Oct 11 — Kapit MP Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi has reminded Village Development and Security Committees (JKKK), associations, and community organisations to manage aid transparently and use it for its intended purposes. “This assistance goes beyond financial support. The assistance includes funding for longhouse administration and management, community activities, welfare programmes and basic community facilities.

items.title: Man, 64, found dead outside his home in Marudi
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 11 — A 64-year-old man was found dead in front of his house in Marudi in the early hours of Sunday. District police chief DSP Nor Aizan Mohd Jamil said police had received a report on the incident. At around 6am on Sunday, passers-by spotted a man lying face down in front of the house and contacted paramedics from Marudi Hospital, who arrived within minutes.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh urges review of Budget 2027 allocation to improve care for older Malaysians in FT
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — Putrajaya Corporation and the Federal Territories Department have been asked to review the allocation they are expected to receive under Budget 2027 to strengthen care and improve the welfare of senior citizens, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh. She said existing approaches must be adapted to the physical and social needs of senior citizens, including those who are bedridden, live alone or have lost their spouses. She was speaking at the Putrajaya-level Federal Territories Senior Citizens’ Day celebration here today.

items.title: Malaysia condemns attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport that killed civilians, injured hundreds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has strongly condemned the deadly attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which killed civilians and injured hundreds. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said the attack had claimed innocent lives and left hundreds injured, while extending his condolences to the victims’ families and wishing those hurt a swift recovery. “I unequivocally denounce the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which has taken innocent lives and left hundreds injured,” he said.
